answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, from the 4 staged assets):

"The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants does not show one uniform prevalence pattern in this Catalonia/Barcelona dataset — its prevalence 'style' switches with habitat and landscape context across three consistent dimensions (composition, per-plot intensity, and per-species spread, set against a temporal surge).

(1) DOMINANT-BUT-SPARSE in semi-natural habitats: In low-disturbance, high-vegetation habitats the gardening pathway is the prevailing component of the non-native flora even though actual invasions are rare. Gardening-introduced species account for ~100% of non-native occurrences in broad-leaved forests (4/4), 87.5% in coniferous forests (7/8), 55.8% in wetlands (29/52) and 53.5% on the coast (23/43) versus 35.1% overall — enrichment 2.9x, 2.5x, 1.6x and 1.5x — and they are present in essentially every invaded plot of these habitats (occupancy 81–100%, mean 1.33–1.44 gardening species per invaded plot). Yet these habitats are only sparsely invaded (3–21 invaded plots per habitat), so here the gardening style is 'dominant but sparse': a handful of deliberately-planted, tall, woody, perennial species that persist locally without spreading widely.

(2) SUBORDINATE-TO-UNINTENTIONAL in anthropized habitats: In heavily managed and human-modified habitats the gardening pathway is abundant in absolute counts (highest anywhere: 45 occurrences in urban plots, 20 in croplands) but is outnumbered by the Unintentional pathway, which accounts for 68.9% of urban and 76.9% of cropland non-native occurrences while gardening drops to 29.8% and 18.5% (enrichment 0.85x and 0.53x; mean gardening species per invaded plot 0.83 and 0.39 vs 1.93 and 1.63 for unintentional). Rock outcrops have no gardening occurrences at all (0/57 plots).

(3) STRUCTURAL-SPECIALIST vs GENERALIST spread styles, plus a modern temporal surge: At the species level, gardening-introduced species are the narrowest-niched (invaded niche breadth 0.449 vs 0.749 for unintentional; marginally significant Kruskal-Wallis p=0.052 with significant Gardening-vs-Unintentional comparison p=0.017), occupy the fewest habitat types (2.0 vs 2.7), are the tallest (mean 6.1 m vs 1.1 m) and are dominated by shrubs/trees and perennials (35 of 39 species), i.e., persistent structural invaders rather than widely-spreading ruderal generalists. Temporally, the pathway is a modern phenomenon: its share of new non-native species rose monotonically from 16.8% (before 1500) to 75.2% in 1985–2019 (397 of 528 recent introductions), a strongly non-random shift (period x pathway chi2 = 230.4, p = 6.3e-47).

CONCLUSION — In context terms, the gardening pathway reveals different prevalence styles precisely as a function of habitat type: it is the prevailing, low-intensity, deliberately-planted route of establishment in semi-natural forested/wetland/coastal habitats where invasions are rare but gardening-dominated, whereas it becomes an abundant-but-subordinate component of an unintentional-dominated invasion assemblage in anthropized urban and cropland matrices — a habitat-context split that is corroborated by the per-plot context model (among invaded plots, gardening presence is relatively more likely than in urban plots in broad-leaved forests, coniferous forests, wetlands and coastal habitats, and less likely in croplands, meadows, scrublands and especially rock outcrops, while surrounding urbanization further lowers its odds) and set against a strong post-1985 temporal surge in gardening introductions."

Supporting statistical evidence (see analysis.py): habitat x pathway chi2 = 75.20, df=18, asymptotic p=5.83e-09, Monte-Carlo p=0.0001 (sensitivity 9x3 without Rock outcrops chi2=74.45, p=1.63e-09); standardized adjusted residuals for Gardening strongly positive in broad-leaved forests (+2.73), coniferous forests (+3.13), wetlands (+3.30), coastal (+2.64) and strongly negative in croplands (-4.11); per-habitat chi-square enrichment significant for broad-leaved (p=0.0066), coniferous (p=0.0019), wetlands (p=0.0018), coastal (p=0.0117) and de-enrichment for croplands (p=0.0003). Sparse cells (broad-leaved n=4, coniferous n=8, scrublands n=5, rock n=1, meadows n=13) are reported alongside every claim as required; the robust pattern is carried by the larger-n habitats (wetlands n=52, coastal n=43, urban n=151, croplands n=108) and the per-plot model.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants shows habitat-context-dependent prevalence styles: it is the dominant-but-sparse pathway in semi-natural habitats (broad-leaved/coniferous forests, wetlands, coastal; 54-100% of non-native occurrences, present in nearly every invaded plot, 1.3-1.4 gardening species per invaded plot) where invasions are rare but gardening-dominated; it becomes abundant-but-subordinate to the Unintentional pathway in anthropized habitats (urban 29.8%, croplands 18.5% share; mean 0.83/0.39 gardening vs 1.93/1.63 unintentional species per invaded plot); and its species are tall woody perennials with the narrowest invaded niches (0.449 vs 0.749), while temporally the pathway surged from 16.8% to 75.2% of new introductions across the four periods - a modern, deliberate, structural-invader prevalence style that contrasts with the widespread generalist style of unintentional introductions.
payload.workflow: Executed analysis.py on the 4 staged assets. (A) Temporal prevalence: 4x3 period x pathway chi-square + shares (temporal_trends). (B) Compositional prevalence: 10x3 habitat x pathway species-occurrence table (invaded_niche n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo summed per habitat, n.total internally verified), chi2_contingency + 200,000-iteration unconditional Monte-Carlo p (sparse-cell robust), Cramer's V, adjusted standardized residuals, per-habitat enrichment vs 0.351 overall share and 1-df chi-square, plus 9x3 sensitivity dropping Rock outcrops. (C) Per-plot intensity/occupancy: mean n.gard and n.unint among invaded plots and gardening occupancy per habitat. (D) Species-level: 77 species after de-duplicating the 4 duplicated=TRUE records; pathway means, Kruskal-Wallis and pairwise Mann-Whitney (Bonferroni x2) on invaded.niche.breadth, habitat.range, n.invaded.plots, AOO, mrt, height, native.niche.breadth; growth-form/dispersal crosstabs. (E) Context model (supporting, descriptive): penalized (ridge) logistic of per-plot gardening presence ~ habitat (reference Urban) + elevation + urban.2009.1000m + cropland.2009.1000m + progressive.1993.2009.50m + log distance-to-road + annual temperature, on all 632 plots and on the 191 invaded plots; penalization used because sparse/zero cells cause quasi-separation in unpenalized ML; coefficients read as directions only. (F) Phylogeny: Newick parsed to verify 77/77 (81/81) species tip coverage; optional Mantel permutation test (9,999 perms) of phylogenetic distance vs |invaded niche breadth difference| among 39 gardening species (r=0.014, p=0.353). Formal PGLS is NOT performed (no R/phylolm in runtime) - trait contrasts are descriptive with the Mantel check as a caveat.
payload.notes: Reported sparse-cell counts alongside every residual/claim: Broad-leaved n=4, Coniferous n=8, Scrublands n=5, Rock outcrops n=1, Meadows n=13; robust conclusions carried by Wetlands (n=52), Coastal (n=43), Urban (n=151), Croplands (n=108) and the per-plot model.
